memories.content: Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the prototype.
Cross-check whether evaluation tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether collected evidence aligns with design and operational decisions to be changed.
Verify at the end that user problems, design interventions, user studies, and expected contributions form a coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions are not linked to prototype functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if evaluation tasks do not produce representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practicality of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Cross-check at the end whether each research question, formative evaluation data, and design modification judgment are seamlessly connected.
Review whether the application conditions of proposed design principles and boundary cases of failure are presented together.
The user can have contributions reviewed only if prototype outcomes and the transferable design knowledge derived from them are separated.
The scope of observation in controlled formative evaluations does not include long-term adaptation and operational changes in real-world usage contexts.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The frames converge on bounding when design knowledge can transfer, while emphasizing different supporting concerns. The reference adds internal-validity and evidence-to-decision checks plus evaluation limits; the compared frame adds a warning about overgeneralizing from one deployment.

relations.reason: These memories express the same one-sided overarching review claim, covering the flow among user problems, interventions, studies, evaluation logic, and contributions.
relations.summary: The reference requires an end-stage review of the overall logical validity and coherence of the submission.

relations.reason: The memories state the alignment check and its consequence for reviewers’ judgments of intervention validity, forming one one-sided claim.
relations.summary: The reference requires research questions to align with prototype functions.

relations.reason: The memories state the evaluation alignment check and its consequence for reviewers’ judgments of evaluation-plan validity, forming one one-sided claim.
relations.summary: The reference requires evaluation tasks to yield representative measures.

relations.reason: The memories state the evidence-to-decision check and its consequence for reviewers’ judgments of contribution practicality, forming one one-sided claim.
relations.summary: The reference requires collected evidence to support concrete design or operational decisions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful, one-sided requirement for detailed research-to-design traceability.
relations.summary: The reference requires traceability from each research question through formative evidence to design-modification judgments.

relations.reason: The reference requires application conditions and failure boundaries, while the compared frame supplies complementary dimensions for judging them: population, environment, workflow, technology, and organizational authority.
relations.summary: Both frames address how to delimit the applicability and transferability of design knowledge.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful, one-sided presentation requirement concerning the reviewability of contributions.
relations.summary: The reference requires prototype outcomes to be separated from the transferable design knowledge derived from them.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful, one-sided limitation on what controlled formative evaluations establish.
relations.summary: The reference limits controlled formative evaluation claims by excluding long-term adaptation and real-world operational change from their observation scope.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided behavioral risk claim, distinct from the shared policy of specifying transfer conditions.
relations.summary: The compared frame identifies a tendency to extend findings from one deployment to all similar organizations.

reports.both: Both require transfer claims to state the conditions and boundaries under which design knowledge applies, including population, environment, workflow, technology, and organizational authority.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame identifies a tendency to generalize one deployment’s results across superficially similar organizations.
reports.reference_only: The reference also requires a focused coherence review linking questions, prototype functions, evaluation measures, evidence, design decisions, contributions, and known limits of controlled formative evaluation.
